data.arc: From June 2025, inflation pressures rose globally as Middle East oil shocks, US fiscal stimulus, and policy debates in Europe and India lifted price expectations. By September‑October 2025, central banks diverged: the Fed began tightening while the ECB declared inflation at target, and emerging markets faced mixed currency and price dynamics. A decisive shift occurred in late 2025 and early 2026 when the US cut rates for the first time in four years, but geopolitical tensions in the Middle East reignited commodity price spikes, especially after the Iran‑US conflict and Strait of Hormuz blockade in March‑April 2026. By May 2026, policymakers warned of a potential stagflationary shock as oil prices surged, leaving the world to brace for sustained inflationary pressures.
